payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- Routine workspace work stays automatic; dangerous operations require consent or refusal.

payload.text:
Audit evidence, 2026-10-06. Installed repository-local Codex config and command rules; no application source changed. Codex CLI 0.160.1, Claude Code 2.1.291, Copilot CLI 1.0.91, Git 2.55.0. TOML parsed, six execpolicy probes passed, and codex sandbox executed true using basicly-consent. Restart is required for project rules to reach the active session. Project settings remain uncommitted and therefore do not yet inherit into newly created worktrees.

Verdict: retain checkout.worktrees/name placement. checkout.py:95-101 implements it for standard repositories. Parallel work requires one working checkout per lane, independent dependency environments, and coordinated shared-state operations. Native app-created worktrees need adoption/provisioning or an adapter; starting a client in an existing basicly-managed checkout is the simplest common workflow. No GUI client was exercised.

Confirmed defects: worktree.py:127-133 returns a FAILED hook message instead of refusing creation, and create persists the session anyway (scratch probe confirmed). worktree.py:136-189 creates the checkout before dependency provisioning, with no recovery/session saved on failure (scratch probe confirmed). A valid Git branch suffix nested/name reaches Git successfully but save_session fails because the metadata subdirectory is absent, leaving an unregistered checkout (scratch probe confirmed). worktree.py:165-170 automatically reads and copies .env.local without a consent flag; no real repository dotenv file was opened for this audit. save_session uses a non-atomic write, cap_refusal reads a count separately from creation, and create/cleanup have no lifecycle mutex or active-user lease. merge.py:347 locks tracker commits; merge_worktree and _merge_and_prove do not hold a repository lock around the landing. Serial iteration within one queue is not coordination between independent clients. base_lock.py:hold_file can steal on age alone, without proving the holder dead. Cleanup preserves unlanded branch content and refuses dirty/unknown status, but uses git worktree remove --force after a status read that omits ignored files, leaving a deletion race and ignored-data policy gap. main_checkout assumes common-dir.parent is the base checkout, so separate Git directories/bare layouts require either support or explicit refusal.

Agent parity: runner.py:142-149 and :393-401 force Codex workspace-write/never, overriding interactive approval defaults; current permission-profile docs establish that --sandbox also overrides default_permissions, losing profile-specific dotenv restrictions. Shared tracker redirect writes from a sibling lane reach outside its working root and require a narrowly scoped permission strategy. Permission projection targets only Claude (permissions.py:14-15); permissions-check passing does not cover the newly installed Codex floor. Command prefixes cannot reproduce Claude infix globs, filesystem deny-read glob expansion has a depth bound (configured 16), and CLI overrides remain stronger than repository defaults. Shared confirmation instructions continue to apply to unmatched variants.

Current sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security ; https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses ; https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions ; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/allowing-tools . Architecture section 18 falsely says Codex cannot set project sandbox/approval defaults; current official documentation refutes it. Worktree-isolation skill claim that Codex has no equivalent native worktree facility is stale relative to installed codex --worktree.

Verification: pytest tests/test_worktree.py tests/test_permissions.py tests/test_permissions_allow.py: 122 passed. pytest tests/test_merge.py tests/test_runner.py: 272 passed. permissions-check passed for its managed Claude list. Full suite,

[session handover 2026-10-06] STATE: Codex consent config installed; activation needs restart. Read-only worktree audit and targeted checks completed; source untouched. Config and audit ledger edits intentionally remain uncommitted. NEXT: persist reviewed settings before creating implementation worktrees, then fix the audited lifecycle defects through isolated tracked work. Exact native enforcement parity and desktop integration remain unverified.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while diagnosing why three of four lanes in one pass reported the size ratchets as a systemic blocker and spent real budget on them rather than on their task.

`python-guidelines` is a **path-scoped skill on `**/*.py`**, so every lane touching Python loads it. Its waiver recipe is stale and the gate refuses the format it prescribes.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml:88` instructs:

> a column-0 `module-size-waiver: <reason>` comment in the file, in the same diff that raises `waiver_count` under `[tool.module_size]` in `pyproject.toml`

Two faults in one sentence, and one omission.

**The kind is missing.** `.scripts/waivers.py` parses a waiver into `COHESION`, `COST` or `UNCLASSIFIED`. The skill's literal format carries no kind, so it parses as `UNCLASSIFIED`, and the gate refuses it - *states no kind, so nothing says whether this is permanent or owed back*. The accepted spellings are `# module-size-waiver: cohesion: <reason>` and `# module-size-waiver: cost(<record-id>): <reason>`.

**The counter moved.** `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml` is the shared anchor that bounced three of five lanes on 2026-08-08 and that `basicly-ef7t` replaced with a per-record `count_delta` in `basicly.d`.

**Rebaselining is never mentioned.** `[ratchet.<gate>.rebaselined]` in `basicly.d/<record-id>.toml` exists for exactly the case a frozen baseline has to rise. It requires a reason and a `base_commit` that is an ancestor of HEAD, it is counted and printed on the pass line, and it is already used **50 times** across 26 entries - `events.py` seven times, `test_loop.py` four. It is the permitted, precedented route, and the file every lane reads does not know it exists.

Verified with a positive control: the file mentions `waiver` five times, and `cohesion`, `cost(`, `basicly.d` and `rebaselin` zero times.

## The cost is a measured lane loss

`basicly-kr7t` was dispatched 2026-08-14 and blocked before a commit; nothing landed. It built the named extraction, measured it against both ratchets, and reverted. It enumerated **all 8.4 million subsets** of the file's 26 natural blocks using the gates' own measurement functions: **225,756 satisfy both ratchets and not one is a nameable responsibility.** The refusal margin was 28 prose tokens - 112 characters. The owner's disposition was *waiver now, decomposition later*, which is the route the skill does not describe.

A median lane is 6.76M tokens and about six dollars. 178 of 447 modules sit within one ordinary edit of a bound, so the exposure is structural rather than incidental.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'waiver_count|cohesion|cost\(|basicly\.d|rebaselin' .basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
2. Read the one hit at line 88.
3. Run the gate's own parser on that literal format:
   `uv run python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.scripts'); import waivers; print(waivers.read_waiver('m','# module-size-waiver: some reason','module-size-waiver'))"`

**Observed.** The one hit is the `waiver_count` instruction; the other four probes return nothing. The parser yields `UNCLASSIFIED` and the gate refuses it.

**Control.** `rg -c -i waiver <the same file>` returns 5, so the probe reaches the file and the four zeroes are real absences rather than a bad pattern. And the `cohesion:` spelling parses to a `COHESION` waiver, so the parser is not simply refusing everything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane reads the waiver guidance, THE FORMAT IT IS GIVEN SHALL be one the gate's own parser accepts, and a test SHALL feed the guidance's literal example to that parser.
- WHEN the guidance names where a waiver is counted, IT SHALL name the current location and SHALL NOT name `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml`.
- WHEN a baseline genuinely has to rise, THE GUIDANCE SHALL describe rebaselining, its two required inputs, and that it is counted rather than silent.
- WHEN the guidance describes a split, IT SHALL state the condition that makes a split satisfy both gates at once, because two in three natural extractions do not.
- WHERE the guidance is projected, THE PROJECTED SURFACE SHALL be regenerated and checked, not only the source.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Feed the guidance's literal waiver example to `.scripts/waivers.py`'s parser and read an accepted classified waiver, against a control feeding the old kindless format and reading the refusal.

payload.text: Verified: hooks.yaml ships pre-commit (identity-guard, pre-commit-script, catalog-lint), commit-msg (commit-msg-script, beads-commit-msg-script), pre-push (pre-push-script), and a Claude PreToolUse agent hook (protect-generated); all three git stages are installed in .git/hooks and every config entry carries an explicit stages: list. Ruling on the rename: .pre-commit-config.yaml is the pre-commit FRAMEWORK's mandated discovery filename — the tool manages every git stage despite its name, and a rename to .hook-config.yaml would break the tool and its editor/CI integrations. payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-E cross-cutting survey 2026-08-14.

Three ratchet gates are three copies of one framework. One copy diverged on the behaviour the merge protocol depends on.

```text
.scripts/check_module_size.py:194     compose(repo, gate, ...)      from basicly.dropin
.scripts/check_noqa_debt.py:216       compose(repo, gate, ...)      from basicly.dropin
.scripts/check_comment_density.py     never imports dropin, reads pyproject.toml raw
config.py:559   "ratchet": _Table(tables={"module_size": ..., "noqa_debt": ...})
dropin.py:109   _delta accepts int only; density baselines are floats, pyproject.toml:291
```

## Consequence

A lane that lowers a frozen prose share, or adds a waiver, has no delta route. It must edit `[tool.comment_density]` in `pyproject.toml` directly. That is the shared landing anchor that bounced three of five lanes on 2026-08-08 and that `basicly-ef7t` exists to remove. The fragment schema fails closed, so nothing is dropped silently today. The collision the fragment system removes is re-opened for one gate of three.

## Acceptance

- When a fragment declares a `[ratchet.comment_density]` table with a float delta, then the comment-density gate measures against the composed baseline.
- When two fragments each carry a waiver delta, then the gate accepts a tree with two new waivers.
- When the three ratchet gates are compared, then all three read their baseline through one composer.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dropin.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `tests/test_dropin.py`
- `basicly.d/README.md`

## Demonstration

Drop a fixture fragment into a test repository and run `uv run python .scripts/check_comment_density.py`, then `uv run pytest tests/test_dropin.py -q`.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on the basicly-zq9i2m pass, log lines `wip: 0/5 unlanded downstream of build; 5 lane(s) admitted; REFUSED: basicly-oqspon` and `dispatch: basicly-oqspon via claude - not started: downstream work in progress is at the [policy] max_downstream_wip limit of 5 (0 unit(s) past build)`. Six lanes were ready, `[worktree] concurrency` is 10, nothing was past build, and one slot stayed idle for a whole pass.

Two sources describe one bound and disagree. `src/basicly/wip.py` (module docstring, "The pass's own admissions count toward the limit") admits `limit - downstream` lanes per pass and refuses the rest. `basicly.toml` `[policy] max_downstream_wip` says the opposite: "Ten lanes may run, and the sixth to finish waits for one of the first five to land ... make review, not slots or tokens, the thing that limits throughput." Requirement 3.1 reads "downstream WIP below limit", which the config comment follows and the code does not. The owner's 2026-08-23 retro named idle capacity as the factory's cost; this bound idles half of a ten-slot pass by design while the review queue is empty.

## Steps to Reproduce

Root with 6 ready children, `[worktree] concurrency = 10`, `[policy] max_downstream_wip = 5`, nothing past build. `basicly loop supervise <root>`: observed 5 admitted, 1 refused naming the limit with 0 units past build. Expected: 6 admitted; a refusal only once 5 units stand in verify, validate or ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN fewer than `max_downstream_wip` units stand downstream of build, THE PASS SHALL admit every ready lane up to `[worktree] concurrency`, and the count of lanes admitted in the same pass SHALL NOT reduce the headroom.
- WHEN `max_downstream_wip` or more units stand downstream of build, THE PASS SHALL refuse further dispatch naming the units to land, as today.
- WHEN the bound is described, `wip.py`'s docstring, `basicly.toml`'s comment and architecture §28.2 SHALL state the same rule.
- Demonstrated by: a test with 10 ready, limit 5, concurrency 10, 0 downstream that admits 10; and one with 5 downstream that admits 0.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `tests/test_wip.py`
- `basicly.toml`

## Context

`basicly-0hxck3` filled the lane card from the three tiers that hold its figures and pushed `board_facts.py` from 3578 to 4219 tokens, 219 over the 4000-token cap. It shipped under a `cost(basicly-<this>)` waiver rather than a split, and this record is the debt.

## Why it was not split at the time

The extraction is real and nameable: `_lane_fact` and its three coercions (`_text`, `_number`, `_whole`) are one responsibility - building one lane's card from the live stream, the last run record and the tracker binding. They would move cleanly.

They cannot move yet because **every one of the 116 modules under `src/basicly/` is named in `.importlinter`'s layer list**, verified by set difference: zero are absent. So a new module requires an `.importlinter` edit, and that file is declared scope of `basicly-rn0o.6`, which was committed and unlanded when this was written. Editing it from a second worktree would have raced a landing.

Prose was cut first and it was not enough: 113 tokens came out of two docstrings before the remaining reasoning was the kind the cap exists to protect. `board_facts.py` is already prose-waived at 58.5%, so density was never the binding constraint here - size was.

## Where it goes

A new `board_lane.py` between `board_facts` and `board_sections` in the layer list. `board_facts` (line 25) imports it; it imports `board_sections` (line 64). `tests/test_board_lane.py` moves with it, because the test-naming gate binds a test file to each source unit.

Expected result: `board_facts.py` returns to roughly its pre-change 3578 tokens and the waiver is removed in the same diff.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run python .scripts/headroom.py | grep board_facts`
2. `grep -n 'module-size-waiver' src/basicly/board_facts.py`
3. `grep -n 'count_delta' basicly.d/basicly-0hxck3.toml`

**Observed.** The module reports over the cap, carries a `cost(...)` waiver naming this record, and the drop-in records the count.

**Control.** `uv run python .scripts/check_waivers.py` passes while this record is open and must fail once it closes with the waiver still in the file - that expiry is the mechanism making this debt rather than an exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the extraction lands, `board_facts.py` SHALL be under the 4000-token cap without a size waiver, and the waiver comment SHALL be removed in the same diff.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL be named in `.importlinter`'s layer list and `lint-imports` SHALL keep all three contracts.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL carry a test file named after it, and the module SHALL be git-added before the suite runs.
- WHERE the cut is made, IT SHALL follow a nameable responsibility and SHALL NOT be a `_part1`/`_part2` split chosen to satisfy a number.
- WHERE `count_delta` was recorded for the waiver, IT SHALL be removed with it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_lane.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `basicly.d/basicly-0hxck3.toml`
- `tests/test_board_lane.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: `basicly-rn0o.6`
- demonstration: Run `uv run python .scripts/headroom.py` and read `board_facts.py` under the cap with no waiver, then `uv run basicly verify --mode full` for the import contract and the test-naming gate.

## Context

Measured 2026-08-28 over `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl`: 72 open records carry labels, and 44 of those labels are single characters (`s` 12, `2` 8, `e` 4, `-` 4, `0` 4, `8` 4). A label is how `basicly loop supervise --label` selects lanes, so a corrupted label set makes lane selection untrustworthy. The shape is a string iterated as a list at a write site: `"phase-2"` becomes `p,h,a,s,e,-,2`. Which writer did it is not yet known; the fold, the import, the seam translator and the kit CLI each touch the field.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `python3 -c "import json;[print(r['record'],(r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels')) for r in map(json.loads,open('.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl')) if 'record' in r and any(len(l)==1 for l in ((r.get('fields') or {}).get('labels') or []))]"`
2. Observe 44 records with one-character labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the writer that split a string into characters is found, IT SHALL be fixed and a regression test SHALL write a label through that path and read back the whole word.
- WHEN a label event carries a value of one character, `ledger-fsck` SHALL report it, so the class cannot recur silently.
- WHEN the fix lands, a corrective write SHALL remove every one-character label from every open record through the seam, never by editing the log, and `snapshot.jsonl` SHALL show zero one-character labels.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/**`
- `src/basicly/owned_store.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_*.py`
- `tests/test_owned_store.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: the reproduction command in step 1 prints nothing, against a positive control that prints the `phase-7` records.

payload.description:
## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 looking at the live wall: "I do not see any factory loop work visualization". Four lanes were running at the time. The board showed none of them working.

## What the operator sees against what the supervisor prints

The supervisor's own terminal, same moment, same four lanes:

```text
running:  basicly-kn4rip 67s 678828 tok [This file already has a family of "refuse a write that recor...]
```

The served snapshot, same moment, per lane, in full:

```json
{"branch":"harness/basicly-6oa3mt","id":"basicly-6oa3mt","live":true,"phase":"build","status":"open"}
```

Elapsed, spend and what the lane is doing reach the terminal and do not reach the board.

## The cause, measured

`board_facts.lane_facts` builds each card from `supervise.lane_view` alone (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:230-246`). `LaneView` carries `last_agent`, `last_outcome`, `last_run_at` and `last_tokens` (`src/basicly/supervise.py`, the `LaneView` dataclass) - every one of them the **last finished run**. A lane on its first dispatch has finished nothing, so all four fold to empty and the card drops the keys.

The live facts exist and are not read. `supervise.inflight_spend()` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:2359`) returns tokens-so-far per running lane and `supervise.inflight_activity()` (`:2366`) returns what each is doing. Both read `_LIVE_LANES` under `_LIVE_LOCK`, which is **process-local** - and since `basicly-bd4epr` the producer is the supervisor's own tick, so it runs in the process that holds them. `_inflight_note` (`:2130`) already calls both for the terminal line.

## The contract has the slots

`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json` declares sixteen keys on a lane: `id`, `phase`, `status`, `agent`, `model`, `live`, `started_at`, `elapsed_s`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, `context_used`, `context_window`, `rework_attempt`, `rework_allowance`, `branch`, `note`. `board_sections.LaneFacts` declares eight and the producer fills five. So this is not a schema change and not a design question - it is a producer filling five of sixteen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running and the tick emits, THE LANE CARD SHALL carry the elapsed time, the tokens spent so far and the activity line, taken from the live stream rather than the last finished run.
- WHEN a lane has reported nothing yet, THE CARD SHALL omit the figure rather than state a zero, on the rule `_inflight_note` already states.
- WHEN a lane has a recorded agent or model, THE CARD SHALL carry it, so a reader can tell which agent works on which unit.
- WHEN the producer is not the supervisor tick, THE LIVE FIELDS SHALL be omitted rather than invented, because `_LIVE_LANES` is process-local and a second process holds none.
- WHERE a field is omitted, THE OMISSION SHALL not be reported to a human in producer vocabulary.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass with a lane running, fetch `/snapshot.json`, and read the elapsed time, the tokens and the activity line on the lane card against the same three figures on the supervisor's own `running:` line at the same moment.

## Context
When a checkout holds git-ignored local folders under a hidden directory, I want pyright-hidden to check only paths that a commit can carry, so local evidence cannot fail a destination verify.

## Finding
2026-11-16: basicly verify --mode full in the base checkout failed pyright-hidden-linux with 122 errors, all in eight ignored, untracked folders under .basicly/usage/ (earlier session evidence). .scripts/check_hidden_types.py runs pyright with include '.' on each hidden include directory. This blocked the landing tool's required destination verify. CI does not see these folders.
payload.title: Check only tracked paths in pyright-hidden so ignored local folders cannot fail verify

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 on the wall board: 'kas8q7 - checkpoint - classify - 1h 54m' rendered in the action band as a NEEDS YOU ask while (1) basicly loop decisions basicly-kas8q7 returned an empty list, (2) the live L3 grant on basicly-xglise delegates classify and ship (preflight prints 'checkpts: classify pending - the live L3 grant delegates it'), and (3) the lane was dispatched and running at that moment under the same supervisor. The checkpoint record stays PENDING until the engine crosses the boundary, so the board derives a human ask from a checkpoint no human needs to answer, and its age clock dates from provisioning - the owner reads a 2 hour bottleneck that does not exist. The one signal the action band exists for trains the owner to ignore it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 on an epic, provision a lane, let the supervisor run it; render the board while the lane is in build. The classify checkpoint shows as a pending ask with a growing age.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a pending checkpoint whose issue is covered by a live grant that delegates it then the action band does not render it as a NEEDS YOU ask.
Given a pending checkpoint not covered by a grant then the ask renders exactly as today.
Given a decision in the queue (loop decisions non-empty) then it renders as an ask regardless of grants.
Demonstrated by: render the board against a fixture with a granted pending checkpoint and one queued decision, and assert the band holds only the decision.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

**Second observed case, 2026-08-23 evening, reported by the owner.** The band read
'2 waiting on a person / basicly-kas8q7 - checkpoint - classify - 3h 45m / +1 more waiting'
while basicly-kas8q7 had been CLOSED for hours. A checkpoint of a closed record is not
answerable by anyone: there was nothing a human could do, no information the board offered,
and no action that applied. The owner's words: 'this seems misleading.'

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 on an epic, provision a lane, let the supervisor run it; render the board while the lane is in build. The classify checkpoint shows as a pending ask with a growing age.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a pending checkpoint whose issue is covered by a live grant that delegates it then the action band does not render it as a NEEDS YOU ask.
Given a pending checkpoint whose record is closed then the action band never renders it.
Given a pending checkpoint not covered by a grant then the ask renders exactly as today.
Given a decision in the queue (loop decisions non-empty) then it renders as an ask regardless of grants.
Demonstrated by: render the board against a fixture with a granted pending checkpoint and one queued decision, and assert the band holds only the decision.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

payload.description:
## Context

The wall layout landed green on its fixtures and clipped on first contact with real data. Measured 2026-08-21 at 1920x1080 on this repository:

- `HEALTH` renders its header and its content is cut off the bottom of the footer.
- The caption under the loop strip is cut to a partial line.

The cause is stated in the lane`s own report: *"the template`s row heights are hand-tuned px against the tallest content each row can hold; a future region gaining a line needs the screenshot re-run, not just the tests."* The fixture carried 12 gate checks and this tree has **36**, so `GATES` grew four rows and pushed `HEALTH` out.

The existing test asserts six fixed rows and one `minmax(0, 1fr)`, which catches a row losing its height and cannot catch a row going one line short of its content.

## Why a taller row is not the fix

A pixel tuned against today`s check count is the same defect one number along. The row has to be bounded by what it holds, or the content has to be bounded by the row with a `+N more` marker naming what was dropped - which is the rule the rest of the page already follows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a region holds more content than its row admits, IT SHALL render a `+N more` marker naming what was dropped, and SHALL NOT cut a line.
- WHEN the gate check count changes, NO OTHER REGION SHALL lose height.
- WHEN the page renders at 1920x1080 with this repository`s own snapshot, NO REGION SHALL be clipped, and a test SHALL assert it against a fixture carrying at least as many checks as the tree.
- WHEN a caption names a count, IT SHALL be fully visible.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: The page rendered headless at 1920x1080 from this repository`s own snapshot, with every region fully visible in the screenshot and a fixture test carrying 36 or more gate checks.

Worse than diagnosed: five of eight regions were clipped against this repository's own snapshot, not two, and four were already one line short on the twelve-check fixture the layout shipped green against, so the thirty-six checks exposed a defect that pre-dated them. payload.description: Quirks bullet proposed from an incident on 2026-09-11. Typing rg -rn <pattern> <path> reads as recursive plus line numbers by habit; ripgrep parses -r as --replace and consumes the next token as the replacement string, so the pattern is silently substituted in every printed line and no line numbers appear. Positive control run this session: rg -rn rank1_floor src/basicly/config.py printed catalog: Table(keys=frozenset({technologies, n, n_high_water})) - the searched term replaced by n - while rg -n on the same file printed 564: ... rank1_floor ... with the term intact. The failure is silent and the output looks like a real finding, which is what makes it worth a bullet: I nearly reported that config.py had no rank1_floor key. Proposal for approval, not applied: one bullet in the non-interactive-shell fragment, which already carries the zsh word-splitting and the count-the-sites-before-a-replace traps - rg -r takes a replacement, never recursion; ripgrep recurses by default, so -n alone is the form.

## Trigger

When a real landing produces a valid lane pytest receipt but the base has a different runtime inventory, I want to establish why pinned setup leaves different runtime metadata and bootstrap code, so I can determine whether the next verification-reuse slice can safely align those inputs.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/provision.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`

## Evidence

The completed runtime slice basicly-rxxtx9k captures actual lane/base payloads and complete runtime inventories under .basicly/usage/pytest-lane-runtime. The base imports basicly source 0.28.0 but importlib.metadata reports basicly 0.27.0. The lane reports 0.28.0 for both. payload.close_reason: shipped by the harness loop
payload.description:
## Context

The harness enforces itself at **commit time**, through 14 projected git hooks. That is one
boundary, and it is the last one: a git hook fires after the agent has already spent the
tokens that produced the violation. The coding agent's own hook surface fires *during* the
work, which is where a cheaper refusal lives.

`factory-loop-requirements.md` section 3.3 argues exactly this for the plan gate — Shingo's
*"source > self-check > successive"* inspection placement, and Theory of Constraints'
"inspect before the constraint". A pre-tool-use hook is the source; a git hook is
successive.

## What must be established BEFORE building, because the docs disagree

Two documents contradict each other on whether the surface even exists:

```text
architecture.md:1871   "Agent hooks for Claude Code and Copilot | shipped"
tier-kit.md:55         on copilot 1.0.77 there is "no hook surface at all: no hooks
                        directory under ~/.copilot, no hook key in its settings.json,
                        no hook option in --help"  -- after three probes
```

`tier-kit.md`'s claim is a dated probe of a third-party CLI, so **both may now be stale**.
The first task on this bead is to re-establish the fact against each vendor's current
documentation and installed binary, per the `interface-facts` skill: never from recall, and
recording the probe so the next reader inherits it. If Copilot still has no hook surface,
this bead ships Claude-only and says so on a consumer-facing surface rather than
advertising parity it does not have — the failure `basicly-irrm` already caught once, where
the README advertised three agents and the ledger held dispatches for one.

## Shape, once the facts are in

Claude Code exposes lifecycle hooks (pre/post tool use, session start, stop). The harness
already owns the checks worth firing there: scope-collision detection, the module-size
ratchet, the plan gate's entry predicate, and the needs-input protocol. Projecting a subset
into the agent's own hook surface makes them refuse *before* the edit rather than at the
commit.

Constraints:
- **The git hooks remain the deterministic floor.** An agent hook is an additional,
  earlier surface, never a replacement — a consumer on a host with no hook support must
  still get the same guarantees at commit time. This mirrors the existing capability-tier
  problem (`basicly-imnu.3`): state the tier delivered, do not imply parity.
- **Projected from the catalog**, like every other surface, so a consumer receives them
  through `basicly install`.
- **No hook may be a silent no-op.** The repo's own root-cause finding is that an
  instrument built and never connected is its recurring defect class; a projected hook that
  the host never invokes is exactly that, so this bead owes a check that the hook fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a host whose hook surface is present, when a projected agent hook is installed and
  the agent performs the triggering action, then the hook runs - check: a test asserts the
  hook is invoked and its refusal reaches the agent, not merely that the file exists.
- Given a host with no hook surface, when the harness is installed, then the delivered
  capability tier is reported rather than assumed - check: `uv run basicly status` names
  which agent-hook surfaces are active and which are unavailable.
- Given the git hooks, when agent hooks are added, then the commit-time guarantees are
  unchanged - check: `uv run basicly verify --mode full` and the existing hook tests pass.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly install` in a fresh consumer repo projects the agent hooks; performing the
triggering action in that repo produces the harness's refusal before the edit lands, and
`basicly status` names the tier delivered.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/**`
- `src/basicly/hooks.py`
- `src/basicly/claude_settings.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none

payload.text:
Copilot half re-probed and settled 2026-08-08 by the owner's question 'will you implement copilot CLI hooks?'. The answer is NO, and not on priority grounds - there is no surface to implement against:

    copilot --version                    GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77
    copilot --help | grep -i hook        (nothing)
    ls -a ~/.copilot | grep -i hook      (no hooks dir)
    grep -i hook ~/.copilot/config.json  (no hook key)

Three earlier probes of a repo-level .github/hooks/*.json also never fired it - on agent delegation, on a shell tool with --allow-all-tools, and on the same without it. Pinned to 1.0.77 because copilot self-updates.

So this bead ships CLAUDE-ONLY and says so. Three consequences for its acceptance criteria:

1. The capability tier must be REPORTED, not implied. basicly-imnu.3 already owns 'declare the tier install actually delivered'; this is the same defect one surface over. Advertising hook parity we do not have is what basicly-irrm caught once already, when the README advertised three agents and the ledger held dispatches for one.
2. The git hooks remain the deterministic floor for every family. An agent hook is an earlier surface, never a replacement - a consumer on a host with no hook support must still get the same guarantee at commit time.
3. Do NOT cite  on the copilot binary as evidence either way. It returns zero for preToolUse, modifiedArgs AND subagent_type - and subagent_type is a positive control that must be present, so the zero is a property of the probe (the 176M bundle is compressed), not of the binary.

What would reopen it: Copilot documents preToolUse with modifiedArgs, so the capability may exist SDK-only rather than CLI-only. If basicly ever drives copilot through the SDK rather than the CLI binary, re-probe. Until then a re-probe on a newer CLI is the only trigger, and it is cheap - the four commands above.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a human on a team that installed only the tracker kit wants to know what is ready and what is holding the rest, I want one command to write a page they can open, so I can answer it without them reading JSON from a CLI.

SPEC.md section 4.3 requirement 10 already commits to this: 'a generated graph and a static board rebuilt on write'. A grep for html, mermaid or svg across .basicly/core/kit/tracker returns nothing, against a positive control that the same tree holds 21 modules and a working CLI. So the requirement is owed and unmet, and it is the last of the competitive claims with nothing behind it.

Section 15 rejects a web application, and this is not one. No server, no network, no third-party asset: one self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and an inline SVG, regenerated on demand, which is exactly what requirement 10 restated the claim to.

The graph must be bounded. This ledger holds 1367 records, and an SVG over all of them is unreadable and enormous, so the rendered subgraph is the dispatchable one - what is ready, what is blocked, and what blocks it - with the count rendered stated against the total on the page. A page that silently drew a subset would be worse than one that drew nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One kit command writes a single HTML file that opens with no network and no other file beside it.
- The page shows the counts, the ranked ready set, what is blocked and what holds it, and every record with its status and what it owes.
- The page carries an inline SVG of the dispatchable dependency subgraph, and states how many records it drew against how many the ledger holds.
- A ledger with no records renders a page that says so rather than failing.

## Requirements

- No engine import, no third-party package, no network, no subprocess, and no syntax newer than Python 3.9.
- The page is one file: no linked stylesheet, no script tag, no external font or image.
- Every figure on the page is read from the ledger, never estimated.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a person files or re-parents a record, I want the tracker to know the record types and which type may parent which, so I can read an epic path that means the same thing everywhere and the graph view can rely on it.

## Evidence (2026-10-13)

- No rule exists: edges.py refuses only cycles of one edge type; issue_type is a free string (fields.py:52), and only the beads importer names five WORK_TYPES (beads.py:30).
- The tracker page offers five types: task, feature, bug, chore, epic (kit/board/web/index.html:167).
- The engine treats bug, chore and task as leaves that build without a plan (src/basicly/loop.py:59).
- The ledger holds 10 values over 1,670 records: task 654, bug 630, feature 171, chore 140, epic 51, docs 17, question 2, research-spike 2, missing 2, feat 1.
- Parent to child pairs in use: epic>task 406, epic>bug 292, epic>feature 91, feature>task 79, epic>chore 48, feature>feature 9, epic>epic 9, feature>bug 8, task>task 3, feature>chore 3, epic>docs 2, epic>question 1.

## Context

Owner 2026-10-13: "you also need to establish the issue type hierarchy or task hierarchy and who can be whoms child or parent from task, feature, chore, epic which i see in the UI. are there other types too?" Feeds basicly-tpr4xre (epic path and dependency graph).
payload.title: Declare the record types and which type may be whose parent, and refuse the rest

payload.text: Owner decisions 2026-10-13 (reply: go, with the type renamed): (1) an epic may parent a feature, task, bug, chore or research record; a feature may parent a task, bug or chore; task, bug, chore and research have no children. (2) Six types: task, bug, feature, chore, epic, research. research replaces research-spike (owner asked spike or research; research chosen as the plain word); docs and question fold into chore; feat becomes feature; any other value is refused by name at input. (3) The 9 epic>epic and 9 feature>feature links stay; new ones are refused. (4) A designer proposes the dependency views on top of this hierarchy.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
Creating or updating a record with an issue_type outside task, bug, feature, chore, epic and research is refused with a message that names the six.
Adding a parent-child edge whose parent and child types the hierarchy does not allow is refused with a message that names the allowed parent types for that child.
The existing epic>epic and feature>feature links still fold and show, and only new ones are refused.
The ledger's docs and question records become chore, feat becomes feature, research-spike becomes research, and the two records without a type get one.
The tracker page offers the six types.

payload.name: requirements
payload.value:
- The rule lives in one place in the tracker kit, read by the CLI, the HTTP API and the page.
- Standard library only; works for a consumer with no engine.
- No new dependency.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner feedback 2026-08-23, watching the live wall while six lanes built: 'there are 6 items in build and all have status open as if nothing is happening. it is impossible to identify what these items on the cards are a part of. having only an ID on the card does not help a human. humans do not memorize IDs. ... There is still too few signals - correct signals - on the board for human to fully trust it and understand what is going on. and the cards probably need to be larger or need to be able to be expanded to see the full messages during work.'

Three gaps in one card:

1. The card's primary status is the tracker record status ('open'), which never changes during a build, so six working lanes read as six idle items. The live signal a human needs is the lane's phase and that it is running now - the epic's design of record already rules this: line one is the phase plus 'started N ago'.
2. The card names only the record id. The design of record already found the join that costs nothing: lanes[].id joins units[].title on every snapshot. The title must be the dominant line.
3. Nothing on the card shows what the lane is doing. The supervisor already holds a per-tick activity snippet per lane (the bracketed last-message excerpt it prints every 15s). Surface it: the card carries the current activity line, and a card can expand to the full recent activity without leaving the wall.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is dispatched and running, THE CARD SHALL show the lane phase and a started-ago duration as its primary state, never the tracker record status alone.
- WHEN a card renders, THE UNIT TITLE SHALL be its dominant line via the units[] join, with the id demoted to a dim address line.
- WHEN the producer holds an activity excerpt for a running lane, THE CARD SHALL render it, and expanding the card SHALL show the recent activity in full.
- WHERE no supervisor is writing snapshots, THE CARD SHALL say the lane is not confirmed live rather than implying activity.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a supervise pass with several lanes, open the board, and compare a card against basicly loop status for the same id: the card says 'open' and an id; the status says build, a worktree and a branch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
payload.title: a lane card shows a tracker status and an id where a human needs a title a live phase and the work in progress

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 1. Commits and gates carry only the human git identity; the runner name/model is known at dispatch and discarded (includeCoAuthoredBy is false). The D3 run-record (.basicly/usage/run-records.json) already holds agent+model per bead; this bead surfaces that provenance as attribution on the landed commit and the gate result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- run_record gains a latest_record(repo_root, bead_id) -> RunRecord | None accessor returning the most recent record for the bead (None when absent or empty).
- The landing merge commit carries agent attribution as git trailers sourced from the latest run-record: Harness-Runner: <agent>, plus Harness-Model: <model> when the run pinned one. No record -> the merge message is unchanged. The conventional subject and the trailing bead id are preserved so the commit-msg and beads hooks still pass.
- The verify gate records the runner: br gate report gets --actor <agent> and the model folded into the note, sourced from the latest run-record, for both the loop landing (loop._record_verify) and basicly verify --issue. No record -> no actor and the note is unchanged.
- Graceful when no run-record exists (verify run outside a dispatch): nothing breaks, no attribution added.
- Regression tests: the latest_record accessor; the merge message with and without a record; report_gate passing actor/model; the loop wiring reads the record.
- Architecture section 12.8 (and the dimension-1 attribution note) updated.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Attribution from the existing run-record only: a merge-commit trailer and a gate actor. No per-agent bot identity (basicly-smzg), no commit signing or tamper-evidence, no new attribution source. Trailer chosen over a synthetic Co-Authored-By (no fake identity/email) per the and/or in the spike recommendation.
payload.title: Identity: stamp the dispatched agent (and model) as attribution on landed commits and gate results

When a fragment declares a scope whose globs match no file in a consumer repository, I want projection to warn about it, so I can catch a rule that will never load before it goes unnoticed.

payload.description:
## Context

Three practices this repo depends on lived only in a session handover and an agent's memory, which
is the exact condition `basicly-ze8z` exists to remove: if you need memory to run basicly
correctly, the repo is wrong. Externalized at the lowest tier each one fits.

Tier 2 (skills), because each applies in a specific situation rather than always:

- `test-discipline` — mutate a fix in **both** directions. Deleting the fix was already taught;
  making the check fire on everything was not, and that is the direction that finds the missing
  test. It found one the same session it was written: a per-lane report labelling every lane
  REFUSED passed the whole file, because no admitted-lane control existed.
- `test-discipline` — restore a mutation from a copy, never `git checkout -- <file>`. A mutation is
  applied to a tree that usually holds the uncommitted change being verified.
- `harness-loop` — a remainder bead is a claim about unfinished work. Two in consecutive sessions
  (`jr0l.53`, `jr0l.55`) were already delivered by their parent and closed with no diff.

Tier 3 (always-on), one line only, because the rule already existed and merely failed to name the
form: `require-explicit-confirmation` listed "destructive resets" without naming
`git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, `git stash` or `git clean`. The omission is not
hypothetical - this session discarded an uncommitted module with `git checkout --` while restoring
a mutation, having read that rule and not matched it to the command.

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on basicly-ibzr0f. The lane judged its change test-only and wrote no `changelog.d` fragment, as its brief allows. The build->verify landing merged green: `release-notes` judges closed records, and the record was still open. `loop run` at ship then dispatched the curator, tore the worktree down, closed the record, and the closing commit `chore(beads): close the shipped track` was refused by `release-notes` (33/34). The record sat closed in the staged ledger with no worktree left to repair in; a human wrote the invisible declaration on main. basicly-mcf2uh hit the same shape on 2026-08-23.

## Steps to Reproduce

Land a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope` and whose branch carries no `changelog.d/<id>.*.md` and no `[tool.release_notes.invisible]` entry. `basicly loop advance <id>` merges green. `basicly loop run <id>` ships, closes the record, and the closing commit is refused by `release-notes`. Expected: the landing refuses before the merge, while the lane still has a worktree to repair in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the landing verifies a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope`, and the rebased tree holds neither `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` nor an invisible declaration for that record, THE LANDING SHALL fail `release-notes` naming both remedies, before the merge.
- WHEN the fragment or the declaration is present, THE LANDING SHALL pass as today.
- WHEN `release-notes` runs outside a landing, ITS BEHAVIOUR SHALL be unchanged.
- WHEN a dispatch brief is assembled for a record that declares a shipped path, THE BRIEF SHALL say that `release-notes` demands a fragment or an invisible declaration at ship for this record, instead of leaving the judgment to the lane.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_release_notes.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_check_release_notes.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
payload.title: a landing admits a lane that owes a release note so the ship close is refused by release-notes

## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on basicly-ibzr0f. The lane judged its change test-only and wrote no `changelog.d` fragment, as its brief allows. The build->verify landing merged green: `release-notes` judges closed records, and the record was still open. `loop run` at ship then dispatched the curator, tore the worktree down, closed the record, and the closing commit `chore(beads): close the shipped track` was refused by `release-notes` (33/34). The record sat closed in the staged ledger with no worktree left to repair in; a human wrote the invisible declaration on main. basicly-mcf2uh hit the same shape on 2026-08-23.

## Steps to Reproduce

Land a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope` and whose branch carries no `changelog.d/<id>.*.md` and no `[tool.release_notes.invisible]` entry. `basicly loop advance <id>` merges green. `basicly loop run <id>` ships, closes the record, and the closing commit is refused by `release-notes`. Expected: the landing refuses before the merge, while the lane still has a worktree to repair in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the landing verifies a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope`, and the rebased tree holds neither `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` nor an invisible declaration for that record, THE LANDING SHALL fail `release-notes` naming both remedies, before the merge.
- WHEN the fragment or the declaration is present, THE LANDING SHALL pass as today.
- WHEN `release-notes` runs outside a landing, ITS BEHAVIOUR SHALL be unchanged.
- WHEN a dispatch brief is assembled for a record that declares a shipped path, THE BRIEF SHALL say that `release-notes` demands a fragment or an invisible declaration at ship for this record, instead of leaving the judgment to the lane.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_release_notes.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_check_release_notes.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
- `.scripts/release_note_standing.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_check_release_notes_landing.py`
- `tests/test_merge_landing.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
- `basicly.d/basicly-18iz59.toml`

payload.text: Confirmed live2026-10-15 while shipping basicly-c25o52c.2: printed loop-run ship token rejected twice within seconds, latest persisted token differed from both printed values. Root cause code: loop._on_verify calls policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded without confirm on every advance, issuing a new token; run_ceremony calls advance before consuming codes, so it overwrites the supplied token. Existing guarded policy checkpoint CLI consumed a fresh token under the already-explicit human ship approval; immediately resumed loop. No gate bypass or new approval inferred. Same defect appears in both basicly-1aj87un and basicly-zq9i2m.1; reconcile ownership before implementing, do not create a duplicate.

body.cause: _on_verify issues a new challenge during advance before run_ceremony consumes the relayed code. The store matches immediately after the first command and changes during the retry.
body.live_consumer: term-qe8sm3 independently reported the same v0.25.0 ship failure after explicit user approval. Public policy checkpoint approval then loop run succeeded.
body.next: Use a side-effect-free approval probe for internal phase/supervisor checks while preserving explicit visible challenge issuance, grants, expiry and one-use semantics. No source changes made.
body.scope: Isolated policy/ceremony integration with actual _on_verify and real confirmation-file issue/consume; ledger and grant decisions replaced by fixture state. No real checkpoint approval.
body.script:
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
import pytest
from basicly import loop,policy
from tests.test_loop import CONFIG,_state
root=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='basicly-confirm-rotation-'))
approved=set()
with pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as m:
 m.setattr(policy,'checkpoint_approved',lambda _r,_i,name:name in approved)
 m.setattr(policy,'approve_checkpoint',lambda _r,_i,name:approved.add(name))
 m.setattr(policy,'record_checkpoint_wait',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'record_wait_request',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'_settle_checkpoint_queue',lambda *_a,**_k:None)
 m.setattr(policy,'_grant_approval',lambda *_a:(None,'',''))
 def advance(*_a,**_k):
  if 'ship' in approved:return loop.AdvanceResult('fixture-i','ship','done','tore-down')
  return loop._on_verify(SimpleNamespace(repo_root=root,issue_id='fixture-i',grant_root=None,state=_state('verify')))
 m.setattr(loop,'advance',advance)
 first=loop.run_ceremony(root,'fixture-i',config=CONFIG)
 printed=first.challenge[1]
 before=json.loads((root/'.basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json').read_text())['fixture-i:ship']['code']
 retry=loop.run_ceremony(root,'fixture-i',config=CONFIG,confirms={'ship':printed})
 after=json.loads((root/'.basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json').read_text())['fixture-i:ship']['code']
 assert before==printed
 assert retry.refused==('ship','invalid or expired confirm code')
 assert after!=printed
 print(json.dumps({'fixture':'isolated policy/ceremony integration; no real ledger or approval','printed_matches_store_before_retry':before==printed,'retry_refused':retry.refused,'retry_rotated_store':after!=printed,'ship_approved':'ship' in approved}))

payload.description:
## Trigger

When one seat learns something another seat needs, I want it appended to the log they already share, so I can deliver it without a mailbox that a crash would lose.

## Requirements

R1. A seat that crashes re-reads what it had not consumed, rather than losing it.
R2. Nothing an announcement carries is invisible to a reviewer or to the board.
R3. No daemon, no second store and no network are introduced.
R4. An announcement that nobody reads is a selection defect that someone can see, not a silent drop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a seat appends an announcement, then it is one event of kind `announcement` in the shared log. [check: `tests/test_events.py`]
- When a seat's brief is built, then it carries the announcements appended after that seat's watermark and no others. [check: `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`]
- When a seat crashes before its next brief, then the same announcements appear in the brief after it resumes. [check: `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`]
- When the ledger consistency check runs, then `announcement` is a known kind and is folded, not warned about. [check: `tests/test_ledger_fsck.py`]

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_events.py tests/test_dispatch_brief.py -q`

## Design notes

Architecture section 31A.5 and D-45. The kind joins the vocabulary of section 32.3, which specifies eighteen kinds and holds ten. The watermark is derived per seat, so a crash re-reads rather than re-receives. Section 8's non-goal refusing agent-to-agent messaging stands for a mailbox and is amended for this form by D-45.

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-26 during the live basicly-zq9i2m pass, 109 s after dispatch, from `curl http://127.0.0.1:8377/snapshot.json`. A running lane row carried exactly `branch, id, live, note, phase, provisioned, status, tokens`. The snapshot schema (`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`) declares `agent, model, started_at, elapsed_s, cost_usd, context_used, context_window, rework_attempt, rework_allowance` on a lane as well. The supervisor holds the agent, the model (`claude-opus-5`, tier `high`) and the dispatch time when it spawns the process, so the omission is not an unknown value. basicly-0xtzf1 shipped the card that draws these fields; with this producer the card draws the title, the phase and the tokens only, and the acceptance clause "show the agent and model the supervisor dispatched" holds on the fixture and fails on the live wall.

## Steps to Reproduce

Start `basicly loop supervise <epic>` with one dispatchable child, then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8377/snapshot.json | jq '.lanes[0] | keys'`. Observed: no `agent`, `model`, `started_at`, `elapsed_s`. Expected: all four present while the lane runs, omitted only when the producer does not hold them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the supervisor dispatches a lane, THE NEXT SNAPSHOT SHALL carry the lane's `agent`, `model` and `started_at` from the dispatch it issued.
- WHILE the lane runs, EACH SNAPSHOT SHALL carry `elapsed_s` derived from `started_at`, and `cost_usd` and `context_used` where the live stream reports them.
- WHEN a value is genuinely unknown, THE KEY SHALL be omitted, never estimated (the omit-never-estimate rule).
- WHEN the lane finishes, THE ROW SHALL NOT carry a live value from the previous dispatch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_supervise_board.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on basicly-0xtzf1. A landing failed pytest and wrote a repair brief. The defect was fixed by hand in the worktree and committed on the branch. The next `loop advance` blocked with `the repair brief for gate 'merge' was written against <old head> and the branch is now at <new head>, so its defect may already be fixed; re-run the gate to raise a brief against what is there now (needs input: validation)`. `repair_brief.take_repair_brief` had already unlinked the brief on that read, so the following `loop advance` landed normally. The message names a step that does not exist, and the block costs one invocation and one human read per hand repair.

## Steps to Reproduce

Land a lane whose verify fails on the rebased tree, so `_repair_in_place` writes `.basicly/usage/repair-brief.json` in the worktree. Fix the defect by hand, commit on the branch, run `basicly loop advance <id>`. Observed: blocked, needs input `validation`. Expected: the stale brief is discarded with a note and the landing runs in the same invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a repair brief is stale against the branch head, THE ADVANCE SHALL discard it, record on the lane that it did and why, and continue to the landing in the same invocation.
- WHEN the brief is not stale, THE REPAIR DISPATCH SHALL run as today.
- WHEN the brief predates the `branch_head` field or the head does not resolve, THE REPAIR DISPATCH SHALL run as today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_loop_repair.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`

## Context
When basicly finds a learning in a consumer repository, I want it to flow back to the main basicly repository with its evidence, so every installation improves the harness.

## Owner intent
2026-11-17, relayed by the Orchestrator in his words: "basicly must be able to learn and self-improve - if it is happening in a client repo, then it must know how to bring back the learning to the main basilcy repo, for example by creating a PR."

## Shape
Shaped with the Orchestrator on 2026-11-20. A consumer recognises a learning only from a recorded fact: a repeated hook or gate refusal (counted by orch errors), a person's correction, or a basicly command that fails or refuses wrongly. A lesson is basicly-scope only when its fix changes a file that basicly install writes; only those are exported. A lesson records no consumer repository name. It closes only by a commit on the default branch of the named checkout. Cuts: .1 shape (this), L1b scope and origin, .2 verified close, .3 orch errors in the kit, .4 export to basicly, .5 pull request.

payload.text: [conversation 2026-11-20] The research session shaped this epic with the Orchestrator. Orchestrator decisions: (1) a lesson records no consumer repository name, and its reproduction command must stand alone; (2) by default the export prints the gh pr create command, and a workspace whose rules allow it may run it, while a plain consumer keeps print-only; (3) the record changes were applied in commit 0d037146. Text fixes: a refused close appends no event, and on success the close event records the repository and the full commit id; the path and user-name refusal reuses redact.py and tracker-path-scan.py, one rule in one place. The INVEST lines below come from a fresh agent with no part in the shape.

payload.close_reason: Fixed in 76f330b: condition-based waits plus monotonic idle measurement
payload.description:
## Context

The three StallWatchdog tests shipped with basicly-kjc5.25 asserted a timing outcome after a fixed time.sleep, so whether they passed depended on how fast the host scheduled a background thread. They passed on ubuntu and windows and failed on macos-latest in run 30168113819, turning main red immediately after the kjc5.25 landing.

Could not be reproduced locally even under twelve CPU spinners, which is the point: a tuned sleep constant cannot be validated on the host that is not failing.

Fixed by waiting for the condition instead of for a duration (a _wait_until helper with a generous timeout), so the assertions no longer encode an assumption about host speed. Also corrected StallWatchdog._watch to measure idle time against a monotonic clock rather than accumulating the nominal poll interval - genuine correctness (a slow probe or an overrunning Event.wait made the flag arrive later than stall_after) though not the cause of the red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the stall watchdog tests when they run on any supported runner then they assert the flag fired without depending on how fast the host schedules a thread, and main is green on all runners
payload.title: Stall watchdog tests asserted timing after a fixed sleep and went red on macos CI

payload.close_reason: done
payload.description:
## Problem

A bead whose `worktree:` external_ref survives the worktree it names is wedged at phase `build`
and no code path can move it again.

`loop_state.derive_phase` reaches the `build` rung on `worktree is not None`, where *worktree* is
the binding parsed from the external_ref - existence of the ref, not existence of the worktree.
So a bead whose worktree was removed without clearing its ref keeps deriving `build` forever.
Meanwhile `supervise.derive_session` adopts it with `live=False`, `ready_lanes` drops every
non-live lane, and `advance_parked` skips on `not lane.live`. The bead is therefore
simultaneously at `build` (so the loop will not re-drive it from intake or classify) and
undispatchable (so nothing ever advances it). Nothing detects or clears the dead ref.

Observed on `basicly-jr0l.4`, which is residue from an earlier session and is re-adopted and
re-discarded on every single supervisor pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly loop status basicly-jr0l.4
ls -d ../basicly.worktrees/basicly-jr0l-4
git worktree list
```

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 at `d31f6bd`, composing the `v0.7.0` release pass. `basicly-jr0l.65`
is a `v0.7.0` blocker whose parent is its epic of origin, `basicly-jr0l`:

```
uv run br dep add basicly-jr0l.65 basicly-yc0x -t parent-child
Error: Validation failed: depends_on_id: issue basicly-jr0l.65 already has parent
basicly-jr0l; clear or replace the existing parent before adding basicly-yc0x
```

Expected — a release cut can be assembled from beads that already belong to an epic.

## Why this blocks the factory's central workflow

`supervise <root>` fans out over the root's **`parent-child` dependents** and takes no
lane allowlist (`basicly loop supervise --help`: the only options are `--runner` and
`--autonomy`). Membership in a release epic must therefore be a `parent-child` edge —
that was the correction made on 2026-08-04 after `basicly-yc0x` was filed with `blocks`
edges and `preflight` reported `0 open child(ren)`.

But `br` permits exactly **one** parent. So a release epic can only fan out over beads
that are **parentless**, and a `v0.7.0` cut assembled from `tcmy`, `jr0l` and `m4zv`
children cannot be run as one supervised pass at all. Measured on this cut: of six
chosen beads, only two (`basicly-cdhq`, `basicly-3yi3`) could be adopted; the four with
an epic of origin (`jr0l.65`, `tcmy.34`, `tcmy.35`, `m4zv.14`) were refused.

The plan's §5 already notes the four beads adopted on 2026-08-04 "had no parent of their
own". That reads as an incidental detail; it is in fact the **only** case the mechanic
supports, and the note should say so.

## Why the three obvious workarounds are all wrong

- **Re-parent under the release epic.** Violates the plan's §14 — a bead's parent stays
  its epic of origin, and phase membership is a label rather than a re-parenting. It also
  destroys which review found the defect, which is the information `tcmy` carries.
- **Root the pass at the epic of origin instead.** Uncontrolled fan-out: rooting at
  `basicly-tcmy` offers 19 open children to routing, which then picks by scheduler score
  rather than by the release's content. That dispatches unplanned, unsized work with
  unmapped scope collisions — the exact defect `basicly-qorx` fixed, re-entered
  voluntarily.
- **Give the release epic `blocks` edges as well.** Refused as a cycle (recorded
  2026-08-04); and `br`'s cycle detection is insertion-order-dependent, so this
  sometimes appears to work.

## Fix shape

The engine side is the cheap half and does not touch the tracker's shape:

- **Give a pass an explicit lane set.** `supervise` accepts the beads to fan out over —
  a `--lane` repeatable flag, or a root plus a label selector (`--label release-v0.7.0`),
  so membership can be the label the plan's §14 already says it should be. This decouples
  "what a pass runs" from "who a bead's parent is", which are two different questions the
  `parent-child` edge is currently forced to answer at once.
- Then a release cut is a label, no bead is re-parented, and the §14 rule holds without
  costing the factory its own workflow.

Carry the one-parent constraint forward as a **requirement on the `v0.8.0` replacement**
(`basicly-vkh0`): the owned work graph should let a record belong to more than one
grouping, because "epic of origin" and "release cut" are independent axes and forcing
them through one edge is what created this. That is a requirement, not a licence to grow
the schema of the component being replaced (plan §10).

## Interim, for this cut

Two lanes supervised under `basicly-yc0x` (`cdhq`, `3yi3`), and the four parented beads
driven as single-track `loop run <id> --root basicly-yc0x`, which binds them to the
epic's grant without changing any parentage (`--root`: "Session root issue whose autonomy
grant may cover the checkpoints"). Correct, and it costs the concurrency on four of six
lanes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
payload.title: A release epic can only fan out over parentless beads so a cut drawn from existing epics cannot be one pass

payload.text:
Narrowed 2026-08-05, same day, after hitting the second half of this in practice. **Grant coverage is not broken - only fan-out is.** The bead's body implied a release cut cannot use the epic's grant either; that is wrong, and the mechanism was already built for exactly this case.

policy.session_issue_ids (policy.py:1293) walks **two** edge kinds: parent-child *dependents* and the root's own **blocks dependencies**. Its docstring states the intent directly - 'A release, or any root that gates work it did not parent, records that work as its own blocks dependencies - a bead's parent is its epic of origin and nothing is re-parented, so a descent-only walk found a session of exactly one bead and the grant covered nothing at all (basicly-jr0l.40)'. It even says 'no set of per-parent grants can substitute for following the edge that defines it'.

Measured here. loop run basicly-jr0l.65 --root basicly-yc0x refused with 'the active L3 grant on basicly-yc0x does not cover basicly-jr0l.65: it is not in that session's issue tree'. After 'br dep add basicly-yc0x <id> -t blocks' for the four parented beads, session_issue_ids returns 14 ids and all four are covered. No parentage changed.

**So the two requirements want opposite edges, and that is the whole defect:**

| Need | Edge that satisfies it | Works for a bead that already has a parent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| supervise fan-out | parent-child *dependent* | no - one parent only |
| grant coverage | root's blocks *dependency* | yes |

A release epic therefore needs parent-child for its parentless beads and blocks for its parented ones, and it can only *fan out* over the first group. That is why the 2026-08-04 correction (from blocks to parent-child) fixed fan-out and silently broke grant coverage for anything with a parent - the two changes look like the same edit and are not.

Adding both types between the same pair is refused as a cycle, so this is a genuine either/or per bead, not a both.

**This narrows the fix**: the engine does not need a new coverage mechanism, only a way to fan out over a set that is not the parent-child children - the --lane / --label selector already proposed. Keep the v0.8.0 requirement (a record should belong to more than one grouping); drop any implication that grants need changing.

## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while exercising basicly-kjc5.59 through `basicly runner dry-run`. Not caused by
that change - reproduced on base `main` with a config that names no tier at all.

`[[runner.agents]]` replaces a builtin wholesale by design, so an entry overriding `copilot`
that does not restate `deny_style` gets `deny_style = None`. But `_inject_copilot_deny_tools`
still injects the permissions.yaml deny list onto that spec, and `format_command` then raises
because `deny_tools` is set with no style to spell it. The result is that **every** dispatch of
the overridden agent fails, including `basicly runner dry-run`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a scratch repo, write `basicly.toml` containing only:
   `[runner]` / `default = "copilot"` / `[[runner.agents]]` / `name = "copilot"` /
   `command = ["copilot", "-p", "{prompt}"]`
2. Run `basicly runner dry-run --runner copilot --prompt go`
3. Observed: `Error: runner 'copilot' sets deny_tools but has deny_style None; known: [...]`
   Expected: either the deny list is emitted in copilot's wire form, or it is not injected onto
   a spec that cannot express it.

The wholesale-replacement stance is deliberate and documented, so the fix is most likely to make
the injection carry the style it needs (or skip injecting when the spec cannot express it) rather
than to re-default the whole spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a config entry overriding the copilot agent without restating deny_style when any
  dispatch of it is formatted then the deny list is either emitted in copilot's wire form or not
  injected at all rather than raising, with a regression test covering the override path

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
printf '\n[loop]\nconcurrency = 2\n' >> basicly.local.toml
uv run basicly loop preflight basicly-yc0x | rg forecast
# forecast: ~84816225 tokens if all 5 lanes start (cap x per-lane)   <- still 5
```

Observed 2026-08-04 - a `concurrency` key written under `[loop]` was **silently ignored**; the real
home is `[worktree] concurrency`. The only symptom was the committed default continuing to apply,
which is indistinguishable from the override having worked at the value it was already at. Expected -
an unknown section or key in a config file this project owns fails loudly.

## Context

Cost a wasted dispatch decision this session: the override was written to bound a pass to what the
grant funded, the forecast silently kept the committed cap of 5, and only re-reading the loader
found it. The failure mode is exactly the one `basicly-23ep` closed for a sibling declaration - there,
`[runner] context_windows` naming an unknown agent now raises, on the reasoning that *a declaration
whose only symptom is the silent default it was written to replace is the defect it was meant to
fix*. The same argument applies to the key itself, not just its value.

The blast radius is wider than a mistyped section. `basicly.local.toml` is gitignored and
machine-local, so a stale or misplaced key there diverges one machine's behaviour from committed
intent with no diff to review and no gate to catch it - the hazard the file's own header warns about
in prose and nothing enforces.

## Fix shape

- Fail on an unrecognised key or section in `basicly.toml` and `basicly.local.toml`, naming the key
  and the sections that do accept it. A strict-schema pass over the loaded tables, not a hand-listed
  denylist that goes stale the next time a key is added.
- Weigh forward compatibility explicitly and record the decision: a consumer on a newer config with
  an older engine would start failing. A warn-then-error staging, or erroring only on a key that is
  a near-miss for a known one, are both defensible - pick one and say why.
- `basicly check` is the natural home; a malformed local overlay should also surface in
  `loop preflight`, since that command exists to answer what a run needs.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Context

Found 2026-08-20 by typing `basicly tracker write -- create --help` to read the verb's help.
It did not print help. **It minted a record** - `basicly-5m2xfd` - carrying one field,
`provenance: engine`, with no title, no type and no description.

`mirror._create_drafts` holds the detection point already:

```text
fields = {"title": positional[1]} if len(positional) > 1 else {}
```

The `else {}` branch is the seam knowing the title is absent and minting anyway. Its sibling
`_close_drafts`, twelve lines below, raises `TrackerDivergenceError` when the argv names no
record, so the refusal pattern is in the same function group and is not being reused.

The upstream half is `br`, which accepted `--help` as a create and replied with a minted id;
the mirror was faithful. That does not make this someone else's defect: the harness seam is
where a consumer types the command, and it is the side this repository can refuse from.

## Why the body gate does not catch it

`ledger-bodies` passed on the empty record - `all 1019 record(s) carry a body` - and that is
the gate keeping its word rather than failing open. Its definition of a body is **a `created`
event exists** (`.scripts/ledger_bodies.py:62`), and the empty record has one. A `created`
event whose payload names nothing is a different claim, and no gate here makes it. Do not
"fix" `ledger_bodies.py` for this; the refusal belongs at the write seam, before the event.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `basicly tracker write -- create --help`.
2. Observe it prints `created: <id>` rather than any help text.
3. Run `basicly tracker show <id>` and observe `fields` holds only `provenance`, with no title.
4. Run `uv run python .scripts/ledger_bodies.py` and observe it passes, because a `created` event exists.
5. Positive control that the seam can refuse: run `basicly tracker write -- close --help` and observe `Error: br close names no issue`, from `mirror._close_drafts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a create whose argv names no title when it reaches the seam then it is refused before any event is appended, naming the argv - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k create_without_a_title -q`
- Given a create that names a title then exactly the events it appends today are appended, so no existing record changes meaning
- Given the refusal then it is raised on the same error class `_close_drafts` already uses, rather than a second one

## Scope

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `.scripts/ledger_bodies.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`

Closed by 3e75b8e7. The refusal reuses the pattern its sibling twelve lines away already had: _close_drafts raised on an argv naming no record, so the shape was in the same function group and was not being reused.

Why the empty record survived: a titleless record is a created event that states nothing, and ledger_bodies reads that event's PRESENCE rather than its content. So the gate that looks like it would catch this reports 'all records carry a body' and is keeping its word - which I confirmed at the time rather than assuming, and which is why the fix belongs at the write seam and not in that gate.

Three shapes refused, all asserted: no positional at all, whitespace-only, and a flag standing where the title should be. Third criterion holds - one error class, asserted by identity rather than by name.

Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4511 tests.

Not found and worth stating: basicly-5m2xfd is the record I filled in FROM the empty record this defect minted, rather than deleting it from an append-only log. So the artefact of the defect became the record of it.

## Problem

`_dispatch_runner` is a fourth dispatch site that D3's spend halt does not cover.
`policy.spend_status` is the one halt predicate, and its own docstring names the three
call sites that enforce it — delegated checkpoint approval, supervised lane admission,
and decider delegation. An interactive `basicly loop run` at the classify to build
transition dispatches a headless agent without consulting it, and without calling
`supervise.admit_working_set` either. So the path a human is most likely to take by
hand is the one path with no cost gate on it at all.

Observed 2026-08-01. `basicly-jr0l`'s grant was exhausted — 43599830 spent against a
21000000 token budget, with `basicly loop preflight basicly-jr0l` reporting
`remaining 0` and `halted: L1 grant token_budget spent ... the session is human-only
until re-granted`. A `loop run` on basicly-jr0l.60 that omitted the `--runner manual`
override resolved `[runner] default = "auto"` to headless claude and dispatched a real
metered agent regardless. The lane ran to completion and committed.

Two things make this worse than a cosmetic gap. The challenge text a checkpoint prints
reprints the command to re-run **without** any `--runner` the operator originally
passed, so relaying a confirm code verbatim silently converts a manual handoff into a
live dispatch. And an exhausted grant is exactly the state in which an operator
believes no dispatch can occur.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Exhaust a root's grant, so `basicly loop preflight <root>` prints `remaining 0` and
   a `halted:` line.
2. Take a leaf bead on that root to the classify to build transition, with
   `[runner] default = "auto"` and a headless agent CLI on PATH.
3. Run `basicly loop run <bead> --root <root> --confirm <code>` with no `--runner`.

Observed: the runner is dispatched and metered spend continues past the ceiling.
Expected: the halt refuses the dispatch, as it does for a supervised lane.

## Root Cause

`src/basicly/loop.py:510` `_dispatch_runner` calls `sizing_at_dispatch` only to
*record* a forecast, then calls `runner.run`. There is no `policy.spend_status` check
and no `supervise.admit_working_set` call, so neither the spend ceiling
(basicly-jr0l.22, basicly-vz78) nor the working-set band (basicly-jr0l.60) applies.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

Widened from the four-line scope this bead was filed with, which named only `loop.py`,
`policy.py` and `tests/test_loop.py` and so did not cover its own third acceptance
criterion: the challenge reprint is built in `cli.py`. Declaring the ground before the
work rather than recording a scope violation at the landing.
payload.title: an interactive loop run dispatch consults neither the spend halt nor the band gate
